look: A tall foyer with a high, water-stained ceiling. A coat rack leans against the wall under a jumble of jackets, and an ornate mirror hangs beside the front door, its silvering gone cloudy at the edges. A stroller is parked in the corner next to a pile of shoes, including a pair of tiny knit booties. A cork bulletin board by the door is layered with notes. Beside it on a small wooden table, a smart speaker blinks a patient blue ring. Someone has left an Amazon box, half-opened, at the foot of the stairs. The grand staircase is a ruin: steps cracked or missing, the banister hanging loose. A stack of fresh lumber leans against the wall beside it.

A coat rack leans against the wall under a jumble of jackets, and an ornate mirror hangs beside the front door, its silvering gone cloudy at the edges. A stroller is parked in the corner next to a pile of shoes, including a pair of tiny knit booties. A cork bulletin board by the door is layered with notes. Beside it on a small wooden table, a smart speaker blinks a patient blue ring. Someone has left an Amazon box, half-opened, at the foot of the stairs. A grand staircase sweeps up to the floor above, patched here and there with fresh, pale wood.

A long wooden table is set for three: two plates and a high chair pulled up at the end, its tray crusted with dried sweet potato puree. Two chairs are pushed back as if their owners stood up in a hurry, and a wine glass lies on its side above a dark stain. A bowl of Halloween candy sits on the sideboard next to a vase of wilting flowers. Tall windows look out over an overgrown garden.

A big old-fashioned kitchen with a cast-iron stove, a deep sink and a pantry door that won't quite shut. The pantry is completely filled with cans and cans of cat food. An empty drying rack sits by the sink. The single-serve Keurig has a carousel of pods beside it and a clean mug waiting underneath. A tall fridge-freezer hums in the alcove beside a kitchen trash can, its bag tied off and ready to go out. A pasta pot sits out on the counter, its lid askew. A plain white cake box sits at the far side of the counter.

An overgrown courtyard garden. Ivy climbs the walls and an herb bed of lavender, sage and rosemary has run completely wild. A dented watering can sits beside the herb garden. In the center of the courtyard, a ring of flat stones marks where someone drew a diagram in chalk, now mostly washed away by rain. A picnic blanket is spread over a patch of grass, and a baby's sunhat lies on it next to a wooden rattle. A row of pumpkins waits by the door. An old, gnarled oak leans against the house, one thick branch reaching toward a small window half hidden in the ivy.

A comfortable room built for long evenings: a deep sofa, two armchairs and a fireplace full of cold ash. The bookshelves hold a strange mix of spiritualism, dimensional theory and home-repair manuals. One armchair has been turned to face a bare patch of wall. A baby blanket is draped over the sofa, and soft blocks are scattered across the rug. In the corner stands a tall curiosity cabinet, its glass doors locked.

A cozy library with floor to ceiling shelves packed with occult tomes bound in leather, books of folklore, and a row of paperback thrillers. A circle of scorch marks is burned into the floorboards, surrounded by scattered objects including a coil of copper wire. A spirit board lies on the floorboards just outside the circle, its planchette resting on the letter S. The air feels charged, like the moment before a storm. An empty cat bed sits in the corner.

A long hallway lined with faded family portraits that don't belong to anyone living here. A roll-top desk stands against the wall, its lid half closed on a pile of papers, and a heavy oak wardrobe looms beside it, a short crowbar lying on the floor against the skirting board. A bad smell has got into the hallway — faint by the portraits, worse by the desk. Baby clothes hang over the railing to dry. Doors lead to a bedroom and a nursery, which emits a soft hum of white noise. At the top of the main staircase, the steps drop away into splintered gaps, blocked only by a solid baby gate. At the other end of the hall, a narrow back staircase leads down to the Kitchen.

The main bedroom: an unmade bed, a dresser with its drawers half open, and a tall mirror over the dresser that catches the light at odd angles. A bottle warmer sits on the nightstand. In the corner, an unpacked moving box labeled HALLOWEEN overflows with costumes, a “Trick-or-Treat” welcome mat and a tangle of fake spider web.

A small, warm room painted a soft sage green. The crib is made up neatly under a slowly turning mobile, and a painted shelf runs along the wall above it, at adult height and well out of reach of anybody small. On the changing table, a baby monitor crackles with faint, happy sounds, though the crib is empty. The sash window above the table looks down over the courtyard and the crown of the old oak. A tin of graphite powder sits open on the sill. A handwritten note is pinned to the wall.
